title: Higher string harmonics
hook: Change harmonic number and predict harmonic frequency.
misconception: harmonic frequency stays fixed when harmonic number doubles.
objective: Apply f_n = nv/(2L) to compare harmonic frequency when harmonic number changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a string fixed at both ends with fixed length and wave speed, f_n = nv/(2L). When harmonic number doubles, harmonic frequency becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model f_n = nv/(2L); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a string fixed at both ends with fixed length and wave speed, with a nonzero initial result. If harmonic number triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on harmonic frequency?
recall.why: Apply f_n = nv/(2L) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
